svg.title: CAPEX is the tip of the TCO iceberg, and the overruns land in the rows nobody budgeted
svg.desc: Above the approval line sit equipment, licences and implementation; below it sit five years of operations, the migration overlap period, training and retirement. The right panel compares the approved and actual spend of the case study by category: hardware, implementation services, operations, training, and dual running during migration, where the last three were never in the project TCO.
svg.text: CAPEX is the tip of the TCO iceberg — and the overrun always lands in the rows nobody budgeted
Case study: a refresh approved at 5.0M closed at 6.2M, a 24% overrun, with hardware price movement responsible for only 0.2M of it
ABOVE THE LINE · what gets approved
Hardware · licences · implementation services
the approval line — the number the CFO signs
BELOW THE LINE · what the project still costs
Five years of operations — often several times CAPEX
Migration overlap — old and new paid for at once
Training, documentation, process change
Retirement, disposal and the decommission work
one TCO basis: equipment + licences + implementation + overlap + operations + training + retirement
Where the 24% actually went
approved 5.0M → actual 6.2M
approval
actual
Hardware
+0.2M FX, components
Implementation
+0.5M night cutovers, decommissioning
Operations (5 yr)
+0.9M never in the project TCO
Training, docs
+0.2M missing entirely
Dual running
+0.4M old and new circuits at once
Three of five rows started at zero. None of them was a surprise
technical event — they were simply outside the approved basis.
The fix is not a bigger contingency
it is comparing the options on one TCO basis before approval, overlap included
A 10–15% contingency covers estimate error. It does not cover entire cost categories that were never estimated — that is a scoping fault, not a variance.
Day-2 operations is usually several times CAPEX, so someone has to represent operations in every design review; nobody else in the room is paid to.
The cheapest moment to find the overlap period, the training line and the disposal cost is before approval, when the options are still being compared.
If two options cannot be compared on the same basis, they are not being compared at all — they are being advocated.
